messages:
sara: Heads up — US-WEST1 queue spiked after the promo. GPU pool hit 92% and latency doubled. Thinking we need a rate-limiter tweak that uses live capacity signal, not static token buckets. Anyone free to sync? :eyes:
vikram: on it. can you paste current numbers? queue length, backpressure counters?
sara: queue ~420 requests, avg wait 3.2s -> tail 9s. Allocated GPUs 48, available heads 4. pod autoscaler not triggered yet. backpressure metrics: admission_rejects +150/min. logs attached (snippet):
sara: ```
admission.queue_length=420
gpu.util=0.92
admission.reject_rate=150/min
warm_pool_spill=23
```
jen: new idea — compute refill_rate proportional to available compute: refill = base_refill * (available_slots / total_slots). Keeps org share but shrinks with saturation.
michael: agree. also consider leaky-bucket smoothing on top so bursts don't thrash scheduler. token bucket gives fairness, leaky bucket for steady drain.
vikram: question: central vs local token store? if we centralize, latency adds. local caches need consistent capacity signal. maybe hybrid: local tokens + periodic global resync + capacity multiplier.
sara: yes hybrid seems pragmatic. local caches hold ephemeral tokens for low-latency, global controller emits capacity multiplier every 10s.
ops-bot: capacity-signal: {region:us-west1, total_slots:48, free_slots:4, headroom_pct:8.3}
jen: propose admission logic pseudocode:
jen: ```
# per-request
effective_refill = base_refill * clamp(free_slots/total_slots, 0.0, 1.0)
if org_tokens > 0 and key_tokens > 0 and queue_len < soft_limit:
  allow()
elif queue_len >= hard_limit:
  reject(429)
else:
  enqueue()
```
michael: soft_limit/history: we should let premium orgs have grace queue credits (small burst buffer) so PLG users don't block critical customers.
vikram: also add model-fallback policy: when headroom low, auto-route to smaller quantized model and mark latency/cost in response header. helps SLOs.
sara: good. header could be `X-Inference-Route: us-west1/quant-4bit` and `X-Cluster-Headroom: 4`.
jen: nit: watch out for clock skew on refill windows if we do token expiry. use monotonic counters or lease tokens by epoch.
michael: rollout plan: feature-flag region-by-region, start with small ratio, and monitor reject rate + tail latency. ops alert if reject_rate > threshold.
vikram: metrics to emit: refill_rate, effective_refill_multiplier, per-org_tokens, per-key_burst_used, queue_depth, gpu_headroom_pct.
sara: question about fairness: if org A uses all tokens, do we throttle org B proportionally? We need hierarchical smoothing: org share * capacity_multiplier.
jen: exactly. per-org capacity = org_commit * capacity_multiplier. If org underutilized, treat leftover as free pool for best-effort.
michael: edge-case: very small orgs get starved by bursts from big orgs unless we add min_guarantee or soft-fairshare. add min_tokens floor.
vikram: implementation detail: token counts in Redis with TTL. For burst smoothing, leaky-bucket can be implemented in local proxy with refill from Redis every 5s.
sara: ops-bot — schedule a short runbook for oncall: how to toggle capacity multiplier, force-fallback, and drain queue.
ops-bot: runbook created: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-rate-surge — admins can set `cluster.capacity_multiplier` and evict warm_pool.
sara: thanks team. can someone prototype the filler algorithm? I'll add perf tests simulating 3x normal traffic.
vikram: i'll take prototype. will post PR with tests and a config example.
michael: :thumbsup:
